seoDescription: Learn how to set up and run live-reload for your Ionic 7 and Capacitor 5 applications on both the Android Emulator and iOS Simulator. This guide walks through the entire process, from initial project setup with `ionic build` to platform-specific permissions for geolocation. Discover critical configuration steps, including setting up Gradle with JDK 17 and initializing Firebase correctly to avoid a white screen. Master the live-reload commands for a smooth, efficient development and debugging workflow.

chapters.title: Essential Gradle & Firebase Configuration
chapters.description: Learn about the critical Gradle setting requiring JDK 17 and the necessary Firebase initialization code to prevent a white screen.

chapters.title: Preparing Simulators & Launching Android Live-Reload
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to open the Xcode and Android Studio projects, start the simulators, and execute the live-reload command for Android.

chapters.title: Verifying Android & Launching iOS Live-Reload
chapters.description: See a live code change update the Android emulator, then run the iOS live-reload command and confirm changes propagate to both devices.

chapters.title: Full-App Test and Conclusion
chapters.description: This final chapter includes a brief test of navigating the app on both simulators, a look at permissions, and the video wrap-up.

summary:
## Project & Environment Versions
- **Ionic Framework**: v7.1.1
- **Capacitor**: v5
- **Angular**: Standalone Components
- **Java**: JDK 17
- **Android Studio**: Latest version required

## Initial Setup Commands
First, build your web assets, then add the native platforms.
1.  `ionic build`
2.  `ionic cap add android`
3.  `ionic cap add ios`

## Platform-Specific Configuration
For certain plugins like Geolocation, you must add permissions to the native projects.
- **iOS (`ios/App/App/Info.plist`)**: Add necessary keys for location permissions (e.g., `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`).
- **Android (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`)**: Add required permissions like `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION` and `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`.

## Critical Environment Settings
Two configurations are essential to avoid common issues.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> In Android Studio, go to **Settings > Build, Execution, Deployment > Build Tools > Gradle** and ensure the **Gradle JDK** is set to a version 17 JDK (e.g., `jbr-17`). An outdated Android Studio might cause errors related to this.

> [!NOTE]
> To prevent a white screen on native devices when using Firebase, add specific platform-aware initialization code to your `main.ts` file.

## Running Live-Reload
The `-l` and `--external` flags are used to enable live-reloading on your local network.

- **Android**: `ionic cap run android -l --external`
- **iOS**: `ionic cap run ios -l --external`

After running the command, select the target device from the list.

## Best Practices & Troubleshooting

> [!TIP]
> Before the first live-reload, it's a good practice to open the native projects (`ionic cap open android` and `ionic cap open ios`) and run the app once directly from Android Studio and Xcode. This ensures all project configurations are synced and dependencies are correct.

> [!WARNING]
> If you encounter an error stating `Java 17 is required, you are using Java 11`, it is a clear sign that your **Android Studio is outdated**. You must update it to the latest version and restart your computer to resolve the issue.
